bull.b: Broad-based double-digit growth alongside premium gross and EBITDA margins indicates strong demand and operating leverage. This combination can support continued reinvestment in products, stores and marketing while strengthening profitability as the business scales over the next several quarters.

Rapid DTC growth improves channel control, customer ownership and mix, while reducing reliance on third-party retailers. A larger direct channel can support stronger margins, better brand presentation and more reliable consumer insight, reinforcing On’s premium positioning over time.

Growth beyond core running footwear, supported by product innovation and scaled technologies, broadens the addressable market and reduces dependence on one category. Successful apparel, training and lifestyle adoption can deepen consumer engagement and create additional long-term growth avenues.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth and promotional conditions may pressure sell-through and make channel performance more volatile, particularly in the Americas. Although management is protecting full-price integrity, weaker retailer momentum could constrain near-term revenue conversion and require further channel management.

A substantially higher inventory balance increases the importance of accurate demand planning while wholesale sell-in is being recalibrated. If inventory growth continues to outpace sales or sell-through weakens, working capital could absorb cash and promotional activity could pressure margins.

Higher import tariffs create ongoing uncertainty around the timing and size of potential cash and margin relief. Because anticipated refunds are not included in current guidance, the company must manage the business without relying on those benefits, preserving less certainty around profitability.
